content.value_statement: Slow Python code wastes compute and creates poor user experiences. This skill guides profiling, bottleneck analysis, and targeted optimization with practical Python examples.
actual_capabilities: Explains CPU profiling with cProfile, pstats, line_profiler, and py-spy.
Shows memory profiling with memory_profiler, tracemalloc, generators, iterators, and weak references.
Compares faster Python patterns for lists, strings, dictionaries, caching, and function calls.
Demonstrates NumPy, multiprocessing, async I/O, and batching for specific workloads.
Provides database query and insert optimization examples for SQLite workflows.
Includes a performance checklist for profiling and benchmarking changes.
limitations: Does not run profiling automatically or inspect a project without user action.
Uses illustrative examples that must be adapted before production use.
Does not replace load testing, production observability, or architecture review.
Some tools require optional packages and platform-specific permissions.

use_cases.title: Diagnose Slow Application Paths
use_cases.description: Find CPU-heavy functions, compare profiler results, and choose focused optimizations for web or service code.

use_cases.title: Reduce Data Pipeline Runtime
use_cases.description: Evaluate loops, vectorization, generators, and multiprocessing for large Python data processing jobs.

use_cases.title: Plan Production Profiling
use_cases.description: Select safe profiling tools, collect useful performance evidence, and avoid changing code without measurements.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Profiler
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Python performance problem and recommend a profiling plan. Explain which profiler to use and which metrics to capture first.

prompt_templates.title: Find Hot Paths
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to analyze a slow Python function. Identify likely hot paths, profiler evidence to collect, and safe first optimizations.

prompt_templates.title: Reduce Memory Use
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this memory-heavy workflow. Suggest profiling steps, lower-memory data structures, and benchmarks to prove the improvement.

prompt_templates.title: Design an Optimization Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a prioritized Python optimization plan for this application. Include CPU, memory, I/O, database, and benchmarking considerations.

output_examples.input: A service endpoint is slow under normal traffic.
output: Recommended starting with cProfile to identify cumulative function time.
Suggested checking database query counts and repeated work before changing algorithms.
Proposed before-and-after benchmarks using representative request inputs.

output_examples.input: A batch job uses too much memory on large files.
output: Recommended measuring peak memory before optimization.
Suggested replacing full-list loading with iterators or generators where possible.
Advised validating runtime and memory changes on realistic file sizes.

output_examples.input: A numerical loop is CPU-bound and runs for minutes.
output: Recommended profiling the loop before rewriting it.
Suggested comparing pure Python, NumPy vectorization, and multiprocessing.
Advised keeping the clearest implementation unless measurements justify complexity.

best_practices: Profile before changing code so work targets measured bottlenecks.
Benchmark before and after each optimization with representative inputs.
Preserve readable code unless the measured speed or memory gain matters.
anti_patterns: Optimizing rare code paths before measuring actual usage.
Replacing clear Python with complex rewrites without benchmark evidence.
Ignoring memory growth while only measuring wall-clock time.

faq.question: Can this skill automatically speed up my code?
faq.answer: No. It guides profiling and optimization choices so you can make measured changes.

faq.question: Which Python profilers does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers cProfile, pstats, line_profiler, memory_profiler, tracemalloc, py-spy, and pytest-benchmark.

faq.question: Does it help with memory problems?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes memory profiling, generators, iterators, weak references, and memory leak detection examples.

faq.question: Is it useful for database performance?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes examples for batch inserts, query plans, indexes, and selecting only needed columns.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill metadata lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it require third-party Python packages?
faq.answer: Some examples use optional tools such as line_profiler, memory_profiler, py-spy, aiohttp, and pytest-benchmark.
